what_it_does:
The rig runs the eleven arms of W10 section 4 on two transports and never mixes them.

Arms, as ids: a, b, c, cctl (arm (c)'s equal-length control, W8 section 4), cprime (arm (c')), d, e, f, r, x, and the optional k. On DeepSeek the step decomposition is file 33's own (S12, S3, S4, S5, S67): arm (a) and its variants (e, f, r, x, k) run as one conversation of five turns, so that the only difference from arm (b) is the carriage and not the decomposition; arms b, c, cctl, cprime run five fresh conversations with a carrier; arm (d) runs a parts pass, then one call per test per part-group, then the assembler. On the Sonnet transport arm (a) and its variants are one subagent working the five steps in order, because the transport cannot share a conversation across subagents.

Mapped to W8's parts. A1 and PA.1: every call saves the body as sent and the reply as returned under calls/<reader>/<run>/, and the run record carries requests, tool_loop_requests and steps, so "one request per step" is a count the record can make on DeepSeek (agreement.py records). A10 and PA.3: exchange.py makes arm (x)'s document, counts every replacement per form, and voids the run if either name was replaced zero times; agreement.py reports arm (x)'s movement both raw and beyond the (a)-to-(a) spread, which is A7's rule that a difference is read only beyond the run-to-run spread. B4: marks.py refuses any criteria field that does not carry a within-step or cross-step sort, and agreement.py reads P4.2 and P4.3 on the cross-step fields and P4.1 and P4.4 on the within-step ones. B5 and P4.5: question.py builds the frozen question by program and arm (f) is handed it with the change list removed, with a gauge that stops the build if any withheld sentence appears anywhere in the prompt. B10 and P4.4: arm (e)'s last call goes to the beta prefix endpoint with an assistant message carrying prefix true and the skeleton, and fixtures/report_skeleton.json names the ports that skeleton sets, which W3 section 8 requires the arm to name; on Sonnet the same text is named in the context and the record says port_set false, the control W10 section 10 describes. B12 and P4.3: partition.py splits the parts under test across calls, "not only the tests", and no test call's context holds the whole parts list. C4 and P4.9: on DeepSeek the rig's own tool loop records every module it served; on Sonnet the workflow script writes the transport's record of tool calls into a meta file; what the reader says it opened is a separate field, and agreement.py records counts the runs where the two differ.

The marker side: first_marker.py builds one prompt per report from A4's frozen criteria.json (designed to <rig>/instrument/criteria.json, schema in CRITERIA-SCHEMA.md), second_marker.py hides and shuffles the reports with the mapping closed in the rig's folder and not the marker's, and agreement.py computes agreement by field and document both between runs and between markers, using W3's P4.1 baseline rule exactly: all three (a)-to-(a) pairs, a document counting as disagreeing when any pair disagrees, tolerance two documents, k = baseline + 3. Nothing is summed across fields, arms or readers, a field whose baseline exceeds half the documents is flagged as saying nothing, and a document where either side has no value is counted unreadable, never as agreement.

predictions_bearing: W10.1 (stage A): the harness dry-runs every arm on one document sending nothing, with the request text saved, for both transports. Met: eleven arms on DeepSeek and eleven on the Sonnet transport, every request written under dry/.

PA.1 (W8 A1): the body as sent and the reply as returned are saved per call, and the run record carries requests, tool_loop_requests and steps; agreement.py records computes 'one request per step in arms (b), (c), (c') and (d)'. Readable on DeepSeek; not readable on the Sonnet transport, which every Sonnet run record says.
PA.2 (W8 A3): agreement.py computes the (a)-to-(a) baseline per field and reports whether it is above zero on at least one certified field.
PA.3 (W8 A10): exchange.py makes arm (x)'s document and counts every replacement; agreement.py reports movement raw and beyond the (a)-to-(a) spread, against four of eight.

P4.1 (W3 s.5): the baseline rule as written - all three (a)-to-(a) pairs, a document disagreeing when any pair does, tolerance two documents - and the flag for a field whose baseline exceeds half the documents.
P4.2 (W3 s.5) and its control: arm (c) against the cross-step fields at k = baseline + 3, with arm (cctl), the equal-length summary that omits the parts list (W8 section 4), reported beside it.
P4.3 (W3 s.5, restricted by W8 B12): arm (d) with the parts under test split across calls, no test call's context holding the whole parts list.
P4.4 (W3 s.5, W8 B10): arm (e) by prefix completion on DeepSeek, with the ports the skeleton sets named in fixtures/report_skeleton.json; on Sonnet the control, recorded as port_set false.
P4.5 (W3 s.5, W8 B5 and B9): arm (f) with the change list withheld and a gauge that it is; arm (c') with the note the writing call wrote, handed on unchanged, note_missing recorded.

P4.6 and P4.9 (W3 s.5, W8 C4): the modules trace taken from the rig's tool loop on DeepSeek and from the transport's tool-call record on Sonnet, kept apart from the reader's own list, with the count of runs where they differ.
P4.8 (W8 C1), optional: arm (k) under file 33 with the router table's rows removed, done in memory with the removed lines written into the run record.

P4.7 (W3 s.5): the S5 step prompt tells the reader, in file 33's own terms, to name a test that cannot bite, quote the sentence that leaves it nothing to reach, and leave the part unknown, so the CANNOT count has something to count.

claims.claim: The skill copy sent to the reader is diffed file by file against HV file 33 before every call, not once per batch.
claims.evidence: run_deepseek.py Run.one begins 'digests = skillcheck.check()'; a counting wrapper recorded 8 calls to check() for a 6-request run. skillcheck.check uses filecmp.cmp(..., shallow=False) over SKILL.md and the seven references, as the old rig does (plan 49 rig, run.py: 'bad = [f for f in files if not filecmp.cmp(...)]').
claims.would_count_against: A run record with no skill_digests field, or a request record whose digests differ from the authority's files at that moment. Both are in the saved request records, so a reviewer can check every call.

claims.claim: DeepSeek's prefix completion needs the beta base URL and prefix true on a last assistant message.
claims.evidence: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/chat_prefix_completion/ read 22 September 2026: 'set base_url="https://api.deepseek.com/beta" to enable the Beta feature', and the last message must have role assistant with prefix true. https://api-docs.deepseek.com/api/create-chat-completion/ read the same day: prefix is '(Beta) Set this to `true` to force the model to start its answer by the content of the supplied prefix in this `assistant` message.'
claims.would_count_against: A 400 from the service on arm (e)'s call. The rig stops that run and writes the service's own words rather than carrying on, so the first live call settles it.

claims.claim: The model name, the effort and the ordinary endpoint are the old rig's, unchanged.
claims.evidence: plan 49 rig, run.py: 'URL = "https://api.deepseek.com/chat/completions"', 'MODEL = "deepseek-flash"', 'EFFORT = "high"'. The documentation read 22 September 2026 lists deepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro, and reasoning_effort 'none disables thinking mode; low / high / max enable thinking mode'.
claims.would_count_against: The service returning 'model not found' for deepseek-flash, which only a live call shows.

claims.claim: Arm (d) as this rig runs it meets W8 B12's restriction: no test call's context holds the whole parts list.
claims.evidence: W8 B12: 'the arm must split the parts under test across calls, as the sketch's own sentence says ("A call handed one test and one part"), not only the tests.' partition.groups returns contiguous groups of at most ceil(n/2) of n parts and refuses fewer than two parts; the dry run built 22 test calls over parts [1,2] and [3,4] and the saved prompts show 'The parts it is to be run on, and no others'.
claims.would_count_against: A parts pass that writes its report or names a pulling pair, so that the whole candidate was assessed in one context after all. partition.leak_check reports every such line and the run record carries them.

claims.claim: PA.1's count is exact on DeepSeek and unreadable on the Sonnet transport.
claims.evidence: On DeepSeek the rig counts every HTTP request and flags the tool-loop continuations apart, so requests minus tool_loop_requests equals steps; the tool-loop test gave 6, 1 and 5. On Sonnet one call is one subagent, and how many model requests it made inside is not shown to the rig; wrap_sonnet writes that sentence into every Sonnet run record.
claims.would_count_against: A transport record that does show a subagent's request count; then the Sonnet field becomes readable and the record's sentence is wrong. The workflow script's meta file already has a 'requests' key for it.

claims.claim: Arm (f) is handed the frozen question with the change list removed and nothing put in its place, and no sentence of it reaches the prompt by another route.
claims.evidence: question.render(q, with_change_list=False) drops both the change list and the stated limits; question.check_withheld raises on any withheld sentence found in the built prompt and is called on both transports. The dry run's arm (f) body contains neither 'Over what range' nor 'Remove each condition the document names as needed', while arm (a)'s contains both.
claims.would_count_against: A withheld sentence appearing in the document itself, which the gauge would catch as a false alarm; the run would stop and the reviewer would have to decide.

claims.claim: The equal-length control for arm (c) is never longer than the summary, and the gap is recorded when the transcript cannot fill it.
claims.evidence: summariser.pair builds the full summary first and grows the control to that word count; the dry run recorded {'words': 267, 'match_words': 322, 'shortfall_words': 55} at the last step, because the fixture transcript had little material outside the parts list.
claims.would_count_against: Real transcripts with a shortfall as large as this one: then the control still confounds length with content and P4.2's control reads nothing. The number is in every summary record, so it can be checked on the first real run.

claims.claim: The modules a run opened are recorded by the rig and kept apart from what the reader says it opened.
claims.evidence: The tool-loop test: modules_served ['reporting'] came from the rig's own loop, with the continuation request's messages system/user/assistant/tool; modules_self_reported came from the reader's text. W8 C4: 'in the transport phase 4 will use, the modules-opened field is the reader's own report'.
claims.would_count_against: The Sonnet workflow script writing the reader's own list into the meta file instead of the session's tool-call record. Then the two fields are one and P4.9 counts nothing; the record's modules_served_by sentence is what a reviewer checks.

claims.claim: The rig's two resume rules hold without sending anything, and a reused call's saved request is not rewritten.
claims.evidence: With send() replaced by a raiser and a fake key in the environment: a run whose record exists printed 'skip' and send was never called; with one call's reply on disk the run reused it and stopped at the next call; the request file kept its original body.
claims.would_count_against: A reused call whose request file's sent_at moves, which would mean the record of what was sent had been overwritten. This was the first design and it was changed.

claims.claim: The rig reads A2's manifest as A2 has written it, and stops rather than guessing where it cannot.
claims.evidence: python3 corpus.py --sources ../corpus/sources.json read 18 sources: exchange as {'exchangeable': true, 'names': ['Fresnel','Stokes']}, why_passage as {'quote': ..., 'explains': ..., 'kind': ...}, split per row as arms/reserve/spare. corpus.py names every accepted spelling in one closed list each and raises on anything else; no digest key is present, so every run record will carry hash_checked false.
claims.would_count_against: A2 changing the manifest after this was written, which is likely, since A2 was still working. The seam is one file, corpus.py, and the run stops with the key it wanted rather than reading a dict into the frozen question, which was the fault this test found.

claims.claim: No file this rig writes can contain a key.
claims.evidence: rig.assert_no_key is called on every write and refused a text carrying the value of DEEPSEEK_API_KEY in the test; the key travels in the Authorization header and never in the body, so saving every body (PA.1) is safe.
claims.would_count_against: A key short enough to appear by chance; the check ignores values under twelve characters, which is a hole a very short key would open.

claims.claim: Arm (a) on DeepSeek differs from arm (b) in the carriage alone, which is what P4.1 is about.
claims.evidence: The saved bodies: at step 3, arm (a)'s request carries six messages of one conversation, arm (b)'s carries two with the transcript flattened into a block. Both run the same five steps under the same system message.
claims.would_count_against: A reading of W3's arm (a) on which the agent must do the whole procedure in one request; then the DeepSeek arm (a) here is not W3's and the difference measured is not M5 (i)'s. That reading is named in the read-me.

dropped.why: Nothing called it: idle. Cut rather than wired, because the digest check it would have forced is already recorded per run as hash_checked, which is a gauge and not a gate.
Both idle. The eight marks and the three provenance words are already written into the arm (e) skeleton and into the criteria file, so these two said nothing that was not said where it is used.

dropped.item: Rewriting a call's request file when the call was reused on a resume
dropped.why: It would have overwritten the record of what was actually sent with a newly built body. Found by writing the resume test; the reuse check now happens before the request is written, and the test asserts the original body survives.

dropped.item: Non-streaming as the default for the DeepSeek transport
dropped.why: Non-streaming gives the reply as one JSON body, which is the truest 'as returned'. Dropped for the old rig's reason, written into its own code: streaming 'captures partial output and the finish reason even when the service ends early' (plan 49 rig, run.py, post()). The rig streams by default and saves the raw stream lines as well as the assembled message; --no-stream is there.

dropped.item: Letting the summariser read a carry-over note as part of a step's answer
dropped.why: The dry run showed arm (c)'s summary quoting the note the fixture reply carried, which would make arm (c)'s carrier depend on which arm wrote the transcript. The summariser now cuts any note block first.

dropped.item: question.for_document treating the manifest's why passage as a string
dropped.why: A2 writes it as an object with quote, explains and kind, and the code would have put the printed dict into the frozen question. Found by running against A2's file. It now takes explains or quote, normalises it to begin with 'why', and puts the document's own sentence into the question block so every arm is handed the same target word for word.

dropped.item: A single arm (d) call per test, with no parts pass
dropped.why: W3's arm (d) hands each call the document, the question and one test, which gives the call no numbered parts to be handed a subset of, so W8 B12's restriction could not be met. The parts pass was added and, because it could absorb the arm's whole result, given a leak gauge.

dropped.item: Treating a field with nothing readable as 'within tolerance'
dropped.why: The first version of agreement.py said a field with no readable pair was within tolerance, and the verdict code then counted None as a loss. Both were wrong: it now reports 'nothing readable' and the verdicts test for False and True explicitly.

could_not_settle:
Whether the beta prefix endpoint accepts thinking mode on deepseek-flash. The documentation at the two addresses read on 22 September 2026 does not say. The rig sends thinking enabled and reasoning_effort high on arm (e)'s prefixed call as on every other, and stops the run with the service's own words if it is refused, rather than dropping thinking and carrying on, which would make arm (e) a different arm from arm (a). One live call settles it.

Whether arm (d)'s split should be cross (every test meets every group; 24 calls a run, 576 Sonnet subagent calls over eight documents and three repeats) or rotate (13 calls a run). Both meet W8 B12. The default is cross and it is a free choice, marked loose; what would settle it is the phase plan's budget, which is not mine to fix. --split rotate --groups N changes it.

Whether A4's criteria file will have the shape the markers read. I designed to <rig>/instrument/criteria.json and wrote the schema down in CRITERIA-SCHEMA.md with an example, and marks.py is the one file that would change. A4 was working in parallel and I did not read a file of theirs.

Whether A2's manifest will carry a digest of the fetched text. It did not when I tested against it, so the runs will record hash_checked false, and a later fetch cannot be checked against the text the runs used. That is a hole in the record, not in the code.

Whether the Sonnet transport's arm (a) confound matters. On Sonnet, arm (a) is one subagent that can revise an earlier step and arm (b) is five calls that cannot, so a P4.1 difference there has two possible sources. On DeepSeek the pair is clean. I could not remove the confound; I named it.

Press first on arm (d)'s parts pass. It is my addition, not W3's, and it is the part of this rig most able to make P4.3 come out right for the wrong reason: a parts pass that quietly writes marks, names a pulling pair or builds a rival has done the cross-step work in one context, and arm (d) then loses nothing because it was never partitioned. I gave it a gauge (partition.leak_check, with the flagged lines in the run record) and the prompt forbids all three by name, but a gauge is not a gate, and the first real parts pass on a real document is where to look. If you think the pass makes the arm no longer W3's arm (d), say so before stage C: the shape of P4.3 depends on it.

Second, on my reading of PA.1. W8 A1 predicts "exactly one request per step in arms (b), (c), (c') and (d)". With the router live, a step that opens a module takes two or more HTTP requests, so I count the tool-loop continuations apart and read PA.1 as requests minus tool-loop requests equals steps. That is a reading, and if the phase plan means HTTP requests plainly, then either PA.1 is falsified by my own design or the router must be off in those arms, which would make an arm difference a difference in what was reachable. Decide which before any run.

Third, on the router being live in every arm. It costs the record's mode 1 (the whole skill in the context), so no run of this round is comparable with the twenty-four subagent runs or the mode 1 API runs on that count. If phase 2's coverage map needs that comparison, the decision is wrong.

Fourth, on arm (e). The skeleton sets four ports, listed in fixtures/report_skeleton.json, and one of them is the report's section order (the part-by-part table first). That is a heavier edit than "a closed list of marks", and it may be the thing that moves the within-step fields rather than the mark column. If you want the lighter skeleton, cut the table and keep the closed-list sentence; the fixture is one file and nothing else changes. I prefilled the last call only, on the reading that the emission arm (e) sets is the report.

The first thing worth doing after this is a dry run on one of A2's documents once the fetcher has written its text, which will exercise the manifest's real shapes end to end; I could only exercise the manifest itself, not a real text.

Sixth, the seams. corpus.py is the whole of the A2 seam and marks.py the whole of the A4 seam; deepseek_transport.py records which client sent every call, so A6's client can replace mine without the record going silent.
